raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Motivation

The current bundle matching implementation repeatedly filters the baseline and target DataFrames for each unique target key, introducing significant overhead as the number of tensor files and unique keys grows.

This PR optimizes bundle matching to reduce repeated DataFrame filtering while preserving matching semantics and target bundle ordering.

Modifications

  • Replace repeated filter_rows calls with dictionary-based grouping and lookup.

  • Group tensor file metadata by identity keys in a single pass over each DataFrame.

  • Preserve target bundle ordering based on the first appearance of each key.

  • Handle cases where the baseline is missing target key columns by matching on the shared subset of key columns.

  • Preserve the behavior of returning empty baseline bundles for unmatched target keys and excluding baseline-only keys.

  • Add regression tests for missing baseline key columns, empty baseline inputs, and target bundle ordering.

Accuracy Tests

Not applicable to model accuracy. This change only modifies comparator bundle matching logic and does not modify model computation or model outputs.

Comparator correctness was validated through unit tests and comparisons between the old and new implementations.

  • Bundle matcher unit tests: 16 passed.

  • Verified matching behavior, unmatched bundles, and target bundle ordering.

  • Compared old and new comparator outputs on synthetic inputs and a real inference tensor dump.

Speed Tests and Profiling

This PR targets comparator performance by replacing repeated DataFrame filtering with dictionary-based grouping and lookup.

Real-world GLM5 inference tensor dump

Evaluated on a self-collected SGLang GLM5 inference dump containing per-module input and output tensors from a single prefill step.

  • Approximately 190,672 .pt file pairs.

  • Approximately 1.4 GB of tensor dump data per side.

  • End-to-end comparator runtime decreased from 1,414 s to 567 s, approximately 2.49× faster.

  • The previous implementation spent approximately 865 s in bundle matching.

These results demonstrate the end-to-end performance improvement on a real tensor-comparison workload. The standalone bundle-matching runtime of the new implementation was not separately reported for this real workload.

Synthetic microbenchmark

The old and new bundle matching implementations were benchmarked on synthetic metadata tables.

Rows per side | Old implementation | New implementation | Speedup -- | -- | -- | -- 1,000 | 0.506 s | 0.0051 s | 99.8× 5,000 | 2.693 s | 0.0255 s | 105.6× 20,000 | 13.907 s | 0.1082 s | 128.6×

For a synthetic workload with 1,323,567 rows per side, the new implementation completed bundle matching in 10.46 s. The old implementation was not benchmarked at this scale.

Synthetic microbenchmark results measure bundle matching in isolation and should not be interpreted as end-to-end inference speedups.

Checklist

  • Format code according to the Format code with pre-commit.

  • Add and run unit tests according to Run and add unit tests.

  • Update documentation according to Write documentations, if applicable.

  • Provide performance benchmark results according to Benchmark the speed.

  • Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

Review and Merge Process

  • Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process, following the PR Merge Process.

  • Obtain approvals from CODEOWNERS and other reviewers.

  • Trigger CI tests using the documented CI commands or contact authorized users if necessary.

  • After CI passes and the required approvals are obtained, ask Merge Oncalls or a user with Write permission to merge the PR.

files.patch:
@@ -7,7 +7,6 @@
 import polars as pl
 
 from sglang.srt.debug_utils.comparator.utils import Pair
-from sglang.srt.debug_utils.dump_loader import filter_rows
 
 
 @dataclass(frozen=True)
@@ -25,17 +24,64 @@ def match_bundles(
     dfs: Pair[pl.DataFrame],
     skip_keys: set[str],
 ) -> list[Pair[TensorBundleInfo]]:
+    """Pair baseline/target tensor files that share the same identity key.
+
+    The identity key is every column except ``skip_keys`` (e.g. drop ``rank``
+    so the same logical tensor on different DP ranks lands in one bundle).
+
+    Linear time: each side is hashed into ``key -> bundle`` in a single pass,
+    then target keys drive the pairing -- a target key absent from baseline
+    yields an empty baseline bundle, and baseline-only keys are dropped.
+    """
     match_key_cols: list[str] = [c for c in dfs.y.columns if c not in skip_keys]
-    unique_keys: pl.DataFrame = dfs.y.select(match_key_cols).unique(maintain_order=True)
+    # Baseline may lack some of target's key columns (e.g. a framework-specific
+    # field in a cross-framework compare); match on the shared subset, exactly
+    # as the previous per-key filter did by skipping absent-column conditions.
+    shared_positions: list[int] = [
+        i for i, c in enumerate(match_key_cols) if c in dfs.x.columns
+    ]
+    baseline_key_cols: list[str] = [match_key_cols[i] for i in shared_positions]
 
-    results: list[Pair[TensorBundleInfo]] = []
-    for key_values in unique_keys.iter_rows(named=True):
-        result = dfs.map(
-            lambda df: _rows_to_tensor_infos(filter_rows(df, conditions=key_values))
+    baseline_by_key: dict[tuple, TensorBundleInfo] = _group_by_key(
+        dfs.x, key_cols=baseline_key_cols
+    )
+    target_by_key: dict[tuple, TensorBundleInfo] = _group_by_key(
+        dfs.y, key_cols=match_key_cols
+    )
+
+    return [
+        Pair(
+            x=baseline_by_key.get(tuple(target_key[i] for i in shared_positions), []),
+            y=target_infos,
         )
-        results.append(result)
+        for target_key, target_infos in target_by_key.items()
+    ]
 
-    return results
+
+def _group_by_key(
+    df: pl.DataFrame, *, key_cols: list[str]
+) -> dict[tuple, TensorBundleInfo]:
+    # dict preserves first-appearance order, matching the previous
+    # unique(maintain_order=True) iteration order (same underlying df order).
+    if df.is_empty():
+        return {}
+
+    col_index: dict[str, int] = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(df.columns)}
+    key_index: list[int] = [col_index[c] for c in key_cols]
+    info_index: list[tuple[str, int]] = [
+        (f.name, col_index[f.name])
+        for f in dataclasses.fields(TensorFileInfo)
+        if f.name in col_index
+    ]
+
+    groups: dict[tuple, TensorBundleInfo] = {}
+    for row in df.iter_rows():
+        key: tuple = tuple(row[i] for i in key_index)
+        info: TensorFileInfo = TensorFileInfo(
+            **{name: row[i] for name, i in info_index}
+        )
+        groups.setdefault(key, []).append(info)
+    return groups
 
 
 def _rows_to_tensor_infos(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[TensorFileInfo]:

@@ -169,6 +169,86 @@ def test_skip_step_groups_across_steps(self) -> None:
         assert len(results) == 1
         assert len(results[0].y) == 2
 
+    def test_baseline_missing_key_column_matches_on_shared_subset(self) -> None:
+        """Baseline dump lacks a key column the target has (e.g. a
+        framework-specific field). Matching must fall back to the shared
+        columns -- the baseline row pairs with every target group that agrees
+        on them -- rather than silently producing an empty baseline bundle.
+        """
+        target_df: pl.DataFrame = _make_df(
+            [
+                {
+                    "name": "t_a",
+                    "step": 0,
+                    "recompute_status": "on",
+                    "filename": "a.pt",
+                },
+                {
+                    "name": "t_a",
+                    "step": 0,
+                    "recompute_status": "off",
+                    "filename": "b.pt",
+                },
+            ]
+        )
+        baseline_df: pl.DataFrame = _make_df(
+            [{"name": "t_a", "step": 0, "filename": "a.pt"}]
+        )
+        assert "recompute_status" not in baseline_df.columns
+
+        results: list[Pair[TensorBundleInfo]] = match_bundles(
+            dfs=Pair(x=baseline_df, y=target_df),
+            skip_keys={"filename"},
+        )
+
+        assert len(results) == 2
+        assert all(len(r.y) == 1 for r in results)
+        assert all(len(r.x) == 1 and r.x[0].name == "t_a" for r in results)
+
+    def test_empty_baseline_yields_empty_baseline_bundles(self) -> None:
+        """Empty baseline, non-empty target: every bundle is produced with an
+        empty baseline side (no match), rather than being dropped.
+        """
+        target_df: pl.DataFrame = _make_df(
+            [_make_row(name="t_a"), _make_row(name="t_b")]
+        )
+        baseline_df: pl.DataFrame = _make_df([])
+
+        results: list[Pair[TensorBundleInfo]] = match_bundles(
+            dfs=Pair(x=baseline_df, y=target_df),
+            skip_keys={"filename"},
+        )
+
+        assert len(results) == 2
+        assert all(r.x == [] and len(r.y) == 1 for r in results)
+
+    def test_output_order_follows_target_first_appearance(self) -> None:
+        """Bundle order must follow the target's row order (first appearance of
+        each key), matching the previous unique(maintain_order=True) behavior --
+        downstream reports are read in this order.
+        """
+        target_df: pl.DataFrame = _make_df(
+            [
+                _make_row(name="t_c"),
+                _make_row(name="t_a"),
+                _make_row(name="t_b"),
+            ]
+        )
+        baseline_df: pl.DataFrame = _make_df(
+            [
+                _make_row(name="t_a"),
+                _make_row(name="t_b"),
+                _make_row(name="t_c"),
+            ]
+        )
+
+        results: list[Pair[TensorBundleInfo]] = match_bundles(
+            dfs=Pair(x=baseline_df, y=target_df),
+            skip_keys={"filename"},
+        )
+
+        assert [r.y[0].name for r in results] == ["t_c", "t_a", "t_b"]
+
 
 class TestMatchBundlesPipelineParallel:
     """Tests verifying that PP works correctly with the existing matching logic."""
